    Equivalence test: is the difference small enough to ignore?

    Source: R/advisor-diagnostics.R
    tv_equivalence.Rd

    A non-significant test does not show that two groups are the same. An equivalence test does: with two one-sided tests (TOST; Schuirmann 1987, Lakens 2017) it tests whether the difference in means lies inside the bounds low and high, the smallest differences that would matter. Equivalence is declared when both one-sided tests are significant, which is the same as the 90% confidence interval (for alpha = 0.05) lying inside the bounds. Uses Welch's t-test, or the paired or one-sample t-test.

    Usage

    tv_equivalence(x, y = NULL, low, high, paired = FALSE, alpha = 0.05)

    Arguments

    x, y

    Numeric samples (y = NULL for one sample or paired differences already taken).

    low, high

    Equivalence bounds for the difference (x - y), in the units of the data, from the smallest effect of interest.

    paired

    Paired samples?

    alpha

    Significance level of each one-sided test.

    Value

    A tv_advice object (question "equivalence") with the difference, the confidence interval, the two one-sided tests and the ordinary test in checks, the conclusion in advice, and result, a one-row tibble with estimate, lower, upper, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost and equivalent.

    References

    Schuirmann, D. J. (1987). A comparison of the two one-sided tests procedure and the power approach for assessing the equivalence of average bioavailability. Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics, 15, 657-680. doi:10.1007/BF01068419

    Lakens, D. (2017). Equivalence tests: a practical primer for t tests, correlations, and meta-analyses. Social Psychological and Personality Science, 8, 355-362. doi:10.1177/1948550617697177

    Examples

    # Is sleep gain under the two drugs within 0.5 hours?
tv_equivalence(sleep$extra[1:10], sleep$extra[11:20], low = -0.5, high = 0.5, paired = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── tidyvisor: is the difference negligible? ────────────────────────────────────
#> Question: equivalence
#> 
#> ── What the data show ──
#> 
#> • Difference: -1.58 (90% CI -2.29 to -0.867) — bounds -0.500 to 0.500
#> • Test against the lower bound: t(9) = -2.78, p = 0.989
#> • Test against the upper bound: t(9) = -5.35, p < 0.001
#> • Ordinary test of no difference: t(9) = -4.06, p = 0.003
#> 
#> ── Recommended ──
#> 
#> Conclusion: Different: the difference is significant and not shown to be
#> negligible
#> Equivalence needs both one-sided tests to be significant (TOST p = 0.989); the
#> 90% confidence interval must lie inside -0.500 to 0.500.
#> Bounds: Justify the bounds before seeing the data
#> The bounds must come from the smallest effect that matters (biology, regulation
#> or earlier studies), set in advance; bounds chosen after the analysis make the
#> test meaningless.
#> For the paper: Report both tests
#> For example: "The difference was -1.58 (90% CI -2.29 to -0.867); equivalence
#> within -0.500 to 0.500 was not supported (TOST, p = 0.989)."
